objective: Replace the failed assumption that one reasoning invocation will naturally remain active for fourteen minutes with an evidence-driven runtime-continuity design and measurable live-retest contract.
acceptance_criteria: Document why plan validity did not produce runtime continuity.
Define separate liveness-production, liveness-detection, continuation, and utilization-measurement responsibilities.
Implement durable state needed to distinguish runtime death from completed work and scheduler delay.
Validate the control-plane changes and leave an exact live-retest continuation.
checkpointable_substeps: Analyze epoch 16 failure evidence and scheduler/runtime boundary.
Research relevant long-running-agent and job-runner continuity patterns.
Implement a runtime-continuity state/measurement contract and validation guards.
Validate and persist the next live experiment.
handoff_boundary: After any completed substep with its evidence persisted.
early_finish_fallback: Audit the next highest-impact utilization loophole and extend measurement/recovery guards without unrelated filler.
progress_evidence: Epoch 16 had a valid ACTIVE plan and passing machine guards but durable progress still stopped at 00:33:25, so plan enforcement is necessary but insufficient for sustained utilization.

External prior art converges on durable execution rather than immortal workers: Temporal records workflow history and resumes after failure; LangGraph checkpoints super-steps and lets workers release; OpenAI background mode supplies an asynchronous runtime primitive for multi-minute reasoning.
Added docs/RUNTIME_CONTINUITY_ARCHITECTURE.md separating wake source, reasoning worker, durable continuation and supervisor/measurement responsibilities.

Updated UTILIZATION schema to count evidenced useful coverage rather than infer work from sparse span endpoints and classified epoch 16 as RUNTIME_INVOCATION_ENDED_EARLY with 145-second invocation span and 779-second continuation gap.
